6. Imported robust mean primitive: clean event and conditional seeds

Depersin--Lecue, Annals of Statistics2022, Theorem2.1, Proposition1, Lemma1 Eq.(6), and Section5 provide the loadbearing interface. Their published Assumption1 generates all independent clean vectors, gives them to an adversary for arbitrary replacements, and permits the selected surviving inliers to become dependent. The mean algorithm is fully covariance-oblivious.

For a fixed score x and n clean iid vectors of mean g(x), covariance <=V_x I, the original clean block event has failure <=exp(-K/180000) and bounds the number of blocks with directional deviation >r_x by 2K/300, simultaneously over every unit direction, where
  r_x=1200sqrt(dV_x/n)+sqrt(1200V_x K/n).
At most |O| blocks change under a replacement. Our K>=600|O| leaves at least119K/120>.99K good observed directional blocks, uniformly over EVERY allowed replacement set and values. The published deterministic rounding argument then establishes its event E_x: for every PSD M with trace1, at least9K/10 observed block means have M-seminorm deviation <=8r_x.

On every fixed dataset satisfying E_x, the source's Section5 proof charges only private covering-SDP seed randomness. With integer u_alg>=1, it returns an estimate of g(x) with error <=808r_x in time Õ(nd+u_alg Kd), failing with conditional probability <=10^(-u_alg). This conditional statement is read from the proof, not inferred from the theorem's mixed statistical/algorithmic failure probability. Thus
  ||g_hat(x)-g(x)||<=B_m sqrt(V_x).                      (6.1)

Zero-covariance/zero-radius safeguard: first test whether at least9K/10 block means are exactly the same vector b. If so, return b. On E_x its distance to g(x) is <=8r_x: apply E_x to the rank-one projector along b-g(x); the two block sets overlap. If V_x=0, every original block mean is exactly g(x) almost surely and at most K/600 blocks change, so the test always returns g(x). Otherwise use the original source algorithm. Sorting exact real vectors costs O(Kd log K), within Õ(Kd). This wrapper avoids a zero-scale division in the source pseudocode without requiring sigma or V_x.

That formula is an explicit computable admissibility test at a given m, but is implicit as a formula selecting m because eps_alg=max(eps,1/m). 2. Direct sufficient conditions with zero-contamination convention

Put B=1+R^2 and W=d_++log(B/delta)+1. Fix the same universal PCA/shift constants as V3. There are fixed universal constants c,C (possibly very conservative) such that the V3 initializer conditions hold whenever
  eps log(e/eps)<=c/B, with 0log(e/0):=0,
  m>=C B^2 W.                                             (2.1)
The projected refinement additionally needs eps<=c_mean and m>=C_mean D_p; (SC),(IG),(RG) can always be checked directly to avoid reliance on an unstated numerical constant. Thus a direct common-sample sufficient choice is
  m>=max(C B^2 W, C_mean D_p),
under the two stated contamination conditions. This replaces the redundant implicit log(1/eps_alg) bound for sample selection; every source-PCA runtime still uses eps_alg, including eps=0.

Proof of absorption, including the floor. For m0=C B^2 W>=1,
  log m0=log C+2log B+log W<=log C+3W,
as B>=1 and W>=1. The function (1+log m)/m is nonincreasing for m>=1. Consequently, for every m>=m0,
  (1+log m)/m<=(log C+4)/(C B^2).                          (2.2)
Since eps_alg=max(eps,1/m) and tlog(e/t) is increasing on (0,1),

  <=max(eps log(e/eps),(1+log m)/m).
